text.p: Following are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
DAWN
- The government has identified 115 public sector companies, including airports, airlines and railways, to be privatised by 1997.
- The cabinet has exempted bonus shares from withholding tax and insurance companies from capital gains tax on shares traded on the floor of the stock exchange.
- Gold prices crashed on the local bullion market on heavy selling prompted by news of oversupply through official imports.
- President Jiang Zemin said China wanted to build a long-term relationship with South Asian states and would never seek hegemony for itself.

- The Supreme Court turned down Benazir Bhutto's plea for an early hearing of her petition against the dissolution of the National Assembly (lower house), opting to decide first whether to admit Speaker Yousaf Raza Gilani's petition.
- Farmers in the Lower Dir district threatened to resume poppy cultivation if their demands for development are not met.
BUSINESS RECORDER

- The World Bank has asked Pakistan to close over 1,000 branches and lay off about 32,000 employees of three state-run banks by December 30 before it considers a proposal to fund the cost of restructuring Pakistan's financial sector on January 21.
- The government will start filing corruption cases against corrupt politicians and bureaucrats this week.
- The government certified that the $1.105 billion Iran-Pak Oil Refinery can start business as a public limited company.
FINANCIAL POST

- Hong Kong will retain its status as an international trade, financial and shipping centre and the legitimate rights and interests of foreign enterprises there will be protected by law, said visiting Chinese President Jiang Zemin.
THE MUSLIM
- The Ministry of Water and Power said there were no plans to privatise Pakistan's irrigation system.
- The Pakistan Muslim League led by former prime minister Nawaz Sharif opposes holding of national and provincial assemblies elections on the same day.
- Talks between government officials and private cellular companies could not be held on Monday, further delaying resumption of mobile telephone services in Karachi.
THE NATION
- The World Bank, Asian Development Bank and OECF have committed nearly $800 million for setting up provincial irrigation development authorities.
- Platinum Bank will open 10 more branches in 1997.
-- Islamabad 9251-274757
